🦝 RaccoonX

 

 Open Source Intelligent Database Inspection & Operations Platform

 RaccoonX is an open-source, cross-platform database inspection and operations platform designed for DBAs, database engineers, DevOps teams, and infrastructure teams.
 
 Formerly known as DBCheck .

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 🗄️ 22 database types 
 🔍 839 inspection rules 
 🤖 AI-assisted diagnostics 
 🔌 Extensible plugin architecture 
 📜 Apache License 2.0 

If RaccoonX is useful to you, consider giving the repository a ⭐.

A Star helps more database engineers discover the project and is one of the simplest ways to support an independent open-source project.

---

 🌐 Project Links

 Website: 
 GitHub: 
 Docker Hub: 
 English: README.md 
 中文: README zh.md
 Issues: 
 Discussions: 

---

 🦝 Why RaccoonX?

Database environments are becoming increasingly complex.

A typical production environment may contain:

 MySQL
 PostgreSQL
 Oracle
 SQL Server
 DM8
 TiDB
 OceanBase
 Redis
 MongoDB
 ClickHouse
 and many other database systems.

Traditional database inspection often depends on manually executing SQL scripts, checking operating-system resources, collecting screenshots, analyzing slow SQL, and writing inspection reports.

RaccoonX tries to bring these tasks together into one open-source platform.

 RaccoonX helps you:

 

It can be used as a standalone database inspection tool or as part of a broader database operations workflow.

---

 📊 Project Milestones

RaccoonX started as DBCheck and has evolved through continuous development and community feedback.

 Milestone Status 
 ------------------ -------------: 
 GitHub Stars 180+ 
 GitHub Forks 60+ 
 Database types 22 
 Inspection rules 839 
 Languages 9 
 License Apache 2.0 

Docker pull counts change frequently and are shown live by the badge at the top of this page instead of being hard-coded here. They represent image pulls and should not be interpreted as the number of unique users or installations.

 ⭐ Help us reach the next milestone

If you have used RaccoonX, tested it, learned from it, or simply find the project interesting:

 Give it a Star. 

 

---

 ✨ Features at a Glance

 Feature Description 
 ---------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 🗄️ Data Source Manager Unified management of database instances, grouping, batch inspection, CSV import/export 
 📋 Database Inspection 22 database types and 839 inspection rules with automated Word reports 
 🔌 Plugin System Independent plugin lifecycle, plugin data, templates, baselines and rules 
 🔍 Slow Query Analysis Execution plans, I/O patterns, lock waits and AI-assisted analysis 
 🔒 Lock Diagnostics Blocking chains, deadlocks, long transactions and remediation suggestions 
 📊 Index Health Missing, redundant and long-unused index analysis 
 ⚙️ Configuration Baseline Compare database parameters against configurable recommended values 
 📈 Historical Analysis Multi-round inspection history, trends and before/after comparisons 
 🤖 AI Diagnostics Local Ollama or compatible cloud APIs for AI-assisted analysis 
 💬 AI Inspection Chat Natural-language interaction with the inspection system 
 🧰 MCP Server Exposes 12 tools (9 read-only + 3 approval-gated writes) to Claude, Cursor and other MCP clients 
 📡 Real-time Monitoring Connections, latency, throughput and availability monitoring 
 🖥️ Server Inspection CPU, memory, disk, network, services and processes 
 🔗 Shareable Reports Generate report links that can be viewed without login 
 ⏰ Scheduled Tasks Cron-based inspection with Email/Webhook notifications 
 📚 RAG Knowledge Base Upload operational documentation for AI-assisted diagnosis 
 📊 Oracle AWR Analysis Parse Oracle AWR HTML reports and generate structured reports 
 💿 DM8 Offline Storage Check Analyze DM8 data files without a running database 
 📝 SQL Editor Interactive SQL editor with syntax highlighting and execution history 
 🖥️ Remote Terminal SSH terminal with multi-tab and fullscreen support 
 📊 Monitoring Dashboard Instance status matrix and topology views; connection/slow-query/capacity drill-down adapts per DB type 
 🧠 Intelligence Center Multi-expert collaborative diagnosis with iterative replanning and reviewer verification 
 🧩 Workflow Orchestration Visually orchestrate inspection actions (DAG) with one-click built-in marketplace templates 
 🛡️ Xinchuang Compliance Compliance scoring by DB type with replacement checklist and mapping 
 🌐 Digital Twin Topology snapshots, configuration drift detection, capacity and health replay 
 📏 Smart Baseline Cross-instance configuration drift detection and capacity forecasting (Fleet view) 
 ✍️ SQL Audit & Write Tickets Write-SQL audit state machine with approval gate (WriteGate): auto-read, approved-write, full audit 
 💾 Disaster Recovery Backup Scheduled database/file backups with retention and health tracking 
 🌍 Multi-language UI Chinese, English, Traditional Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, French, German and Russian 

---

 🗄️ Supported Databases

RaccoonX currently supports 22 database and data systems .

 ------------- ----------------------- -----------: --------------------------

 MariaDB pymysql 3306 10.3+

 Oracle oracledb / JPype1 + ojdbc 1521 11g R2 / 12c / 19c / 21c+, native or JDBC 
 SQL Server pyodbc / JDBC 1433 2012+, native or JDBC 
 DM8 dmpython 5236 Dameng 
 TiDB pymysql 4000 MySQL protocol 
 IvorySQL psycopg2 5333 PostgreSQL compatible 
 YashanDB yashandb 1688 Oracle compatible 
 KingbaseES psycopg2 54321 PostgreSQL compatible 
 GBase 8s JDBC 9088 JDK + JDBC 
 UXDB JDBC 33060 PostgreSQL compatible 
 HGDB (HighGo) JDBC 5866 PostgreSQL compatible 
 Vastbase G100 JDBC 5432 Vastbase, openGauss kernel 
 HaloDB JDBC 5432 Xihe Data, PG/Oracle dual-compatible 
 GBase 8a JDBC 5258 Column-store warehouse 
 MongoDB pymongo 27017 4.0+

install.title: Quick Start
install.html:
🐳 Docker — Recommended

Docker is the easiest way to start RaccoonX.

Docker Images
docker pull jackge12345/dbcheck:latest

docker run -d -p 5003:5003 \
  -v dbcheck_data:/app/data \
  -v dbcheck_reports:/app/data/reports \
  -e LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/dmssl \
  jackge12345/dbcheck:latest
GitHub Container Registry
docker pull ghcr.io/fiyo/dbcheck:latest

docker run -d -p 5003:5003 \
  -v dbcheck_data:/app/data \
  -v dbcheck_reports:/app/data/reports \
  -e LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/dmssl \
  ghcr.io/fiyo/dbcheck:latest

Open:

http://localhost:5003

Default credentials:

Username: admin
Password: admin123

Please change the password after the first login.

🐳 Docker Compose

curl -o deploy/docker-compose.yml \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fiyo/DBCheck/main/deploy/docker-compose.yml

docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml up -d

GBase 8s

The Docker image includes the required JDK and JDBC driver. GBase 8s can be used without additional driver installation when running through the provided image.

🐧 Kylin / ARM64 domestic server deployment

The official image is a multi-architecture image (linux/amd64 + linux/arm64). docker pull picks the right one automatically, so Kylin servers reporting aarch64 from uname -m (Kunpeng 920 / Phytium S2500, S5000C) work out of the box.

The image ships its own user-space runtime (Debian 12 / glibc 2.36), isolated from the host's glibc, so the host only needs kernel ≥ 4.x — Galaxy Kylin V10 SP3 ships kernel 4.19.90 and fully qualifies.

uname -m                                      # expect aarch64
# Version list: https://github.com/fiyo/DBCheck/releases
VERSION=26.11.13.1
docker pull jackge12345/dbcheck:$VERSION     # pin an explicit version
docker run -d -p 5003:5003 \
  --memory=2g --memory-swap=2g \
  -v dbcheck_data:/app/data \
  -v dbcheck_reports:/app/reports \
  --name raccoonx \
  jackge12345/dbcheck:$VERSION

Pin an explicit version tag

latest may still point at an older single-architecture image. If the pull fails with no matching manifest for linux/arm64, retry with a pinned version.

Driver differences on arm64

Database arm64 Notes
MySQL / MariaDB / TiDB / OceanBase / TDSQL-C ✅ Pure-Python drivers, architecture independent
PostgreSQL family (IvorySQL, Kingbase, UXDB, HGDB, Vastbase, HaloDB) ✅ psycopg2 is architecture independent
DM8 (Dameng) ✅ Uses the pure-Java JDBC driver in the image, no native client needed
YashanDB ✅ Driver is a pure-Python wheel (py3-none-any)
MongoDB / Redis / ClickHouse ✅ Architecture independent
SQL Server ⚠️ Install msodbcsql18 yourself (the image ships only the unixodbc driver manager)
Oracle ⚠️ Thick mode needs the x86_64 Instant Client and is unavailable on arm64; thin mode and the oracle_jdbc path work
GBase 8s ⚠️ The native Python driver needs the GBase SDK — use the JDBC path on arm64

Pick the right install method for Kylin / ARM64 servers

Linux binaries are published for x86_64 and aarch64, both built in manylinux_2_28 containers and requiring glibc >= 2.28. Pick by uname -m:

  • x86_64 -> RaccoonX-Linux-x86_64-*.tar.gz (Galaxy Kylin V10 SP3 x86_64)
  • aarch64 -> RaccoonX-Linux-aarch64-*.tar.gz (Kunpeng 920 / Phytium, Kylin V10 arm64)

Unpack and run bash start.sh. Older glibc 2.17 systems (CentOS 7) still need the multi-arch image above; Oracle thick / GBase native drivers remain x86_64-only. Do not build on a newer glibc host and copy the binary over: GLIBC_2.34 not found.
